hypothesis: Where whole routes are too constrained by the protected state mask, test contiguous admissible 5-10-parent segments linking near-target decisions without exposing protected stars.
supervision: Exact shortest-path segments translated toward absolute near-solved targets. Every parent and all candidates in every segment satisfy the original relation and state exclusions. A segment can end before the target; report it as segment supervision, not a complete-route success.
comparison: Keep the low-learning-rate baseline's Q, Adam, losses, restoration replay, update budget and candidate-selection rule. Change only near-target sampling to a fixed admissible segment pool, including repeated exposure; report its actual support and sampled star counts.
scope: Bounded segment-data continuation from step 1000, with all stage checkpoints retained. No automatic extension, loosening of heldout exclusions or adoption.
